title: POC Weekly Sync - Quality Eval & Regression Checks
summary: Weekly POC sync to review evaluation results, confirm regression checks for prompt sets, discuss guardrails and scoring thresholds, and align on next steps for dedicated latency benchmarking and SOC2/security docs.
next_steps: Redwood to send updated prompt set and scoring spreadsheet
Redwood SE to run dedicated latency benchmark and share logs
Customer to provide 200 additional eval prompts and edge cases
Schedule follow-up demo for guardrail integration (canary flow)
action_items: Maya Patel - Send updated prompt set + scoring spreadsheet - due 2025-07-10
Ethan Chen - Run Dedicated latency benchmark (p50/p95/p99) and share logs - due 2025-07-15
Amira Khan - Provide 200 eval prompts and edge-case examples - due 2025-07-11
Jia Li - Share current infra diagram and VPC networking constraints - due 2025-07-12
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to keep this tight, about 40 minutes. Um, quick roll call?
[00:00:12] Amira: Hi, Amira here from NimbleDocs, ML lead.
[00:00:15] Sam: Sam, product.
[00:00:18] Jia: Jia, SRE.
[00:00:20] Maya: Great. Ethan from Redwood?
[00:00:23] Ethan: Yep, Ethan Chen, solutions engineering.
[00:00:27] Maya: Cool. Quick agenda: review last week's eval results, look for regressions across prompt sets, confirm guardrail behaviour, and decide next steps for benchmarking on Dedicated.
[00:00:35] Sam: Sounds good. We did the run you sent against 1k prompts, right?
[00:00:40] Ethan: Yes, 1,024 prompts. We ran against model v1.3 and the quantized v1.3-q, and then fallback to hosted for a small slice.
[00:00:52] Amira: Quick note — a couple of the labels looked off, like entity extraction examples were mis-labeled in the spreadsheet, maybe transcription?
[00:00:58] Maya: Yeah there were a few mis-annotations, we fixed the scoring mapping and uploaded a corrected CSV to the drive (link shared in chat).
[00:01:10] Jia: We care about false positives more than negatives on our use-case, so thresholding matters.
[00:01:16] Ethan: Right, that's what we tuned — the scoring pipeline now weights precision heavier for the extraction set.
[00:01:24] Maya: Walk us through the regression checks — what did we see?
[00:01:29] Ethan: Overall, v1.3 had 93% accuracy on the core intent prompts, v1.3-q dropped to 90%, but latency improved by ~38% on average; however we saw a 6% regression on edge-case prompts where context window is long, likely due to quantization dropping rare-token fidelity.
[00:01:52] Amira: That's the worry — our long-doc summarization flows hit those edge tokens. Can guardrails help us detect low-confidence outputs?
[00:01:59] Ethan: Yes — we prototyped a confidence scorer based on log-prob aggregation and a secondary reranker. When confidence is low we either surface a flag or fall back to hosted higher-precision model. That's the fallback policy we demoed.
[00:02:15] Sam: What's the tradeoff on cost if we fallback to hosted frequently?
[00:02:19] Maya: We estimated unit cost bump of roughly 2.3x for those fallbacks, but overall cost stays lower if fallback is rare. We'll add thresholds to control that.
[00:02:29] Jia: From infra, we want to know about KV cache invalidation and prefix caching — some prompts have session carryover, we can't leak across tenants.
[00:02:37] Ethan: Absolutely, we enforce per-tenant KV namespaces, and cache TTLs are configurable. We also have audit logs for cache reads/writes (we can share a sample).
[00:02:47] Amira: Security checklist — we need SOC 2 + SSO/SAML details for the security review next week.
[00:02:53] Maya: We'll send SOC 2 report, SAML config docs, and the deployment diagram.
[00:02:57] Sam: Back to scoring, can you show an example prompt that regressed?
[00:03:02] Ethan: Sure, I'll read one: (reads) "Summarize the following 4,500-word legal memo focusing on implied terms and exclusions" — v1.3 returned concise points, v1.3-q dropped a key clause twice. The scorer flagged low confidence.
[00:03:20] Amira: Hmm. For legal it's critical. Can we increase beam or nctx to help?
[00:03:25] Ethan: On Dedicated we can bump kv cache and context handling, but that increases memory per replica. That's why Dedicated capacity sometimes required.
[00:03:33] Maya: This ties into the Dedicated vs Hosted decision — if you want consistent p99 latency and higher fidelity on long contexts, Dedicated is recommended. Hosted is fine for most standard flows.
[00:03:44] Sam: What's the expected p95 on Dedicated?
[00:03:47] Ethan: Our initial numbers: p50 ~ 60ms/token, p95 ~ 220ms/token for the optimized runtime on A100-style hardware; quantized knocks latency down but can affect p99 tail and quality. We'll run a Dedicated benchmark and give you p50/p95/p99 numbers for your exact prompt distribution.
[00:04:05] Jia: Please include warm vs cold cache numbers. Cold starts are where we see spikes.
[00:04:10] Ethan: Will do — we'll capture cold/warm, and request sizes.
[00:04:14] Maya: Quick check on guardrails — do we have safety filters and output format enforcement?
[00:04:18] Ethan: Yes, we can apply both pre-output classifiers and post-output schema validators. For your extraction flows we recommend a JSON schema validator to avoid malformed outputs.
[00:04:29] Amira: Great. On the scoring spreadsheet — we had suggestions for weights per task, can you incorporate them?
[00:04:34] Maya: We already merged the suggested weights for extraction and classification, will send updated version after this call.
[00:04:40] Sam: Also curious about rollout — can we canary 10% of traffic to Dedicated variant?
[00:04:45] Ethan: Yes, rollout policies support canary and A/B with automatic rollback triggers based on error rates and quality regressions tied to eval prompts. We can set up automatic rollback if precision drops below threshold.
[00:04:58] Jia: About logs — we need redaction for PII, we can't have raw user text in logs.
[00:05:04] Ethan: Redwood supports configurable redaction and token-level anonymization; raw transcripts can be disabled in audit logs per customer.
[00:05:12] Amira: Good. Any open regressions you want us to triage?
[00:05:16] Ethan: The main one is the 6% regression on long-context edge cases with quantized model; another is occasional hallucination on numeric tables. We think both are addressable with prompt framing and a small reranker.
[00:05:29] Maya: Okay let's plan: Redwood sends updated prompts and scoring sheet, SE runs dedicated benchmarks, customer provides 200 additional edge prompts.
[00:05:36] Sam: Timeline — can we get the benchmark results by next Tuesday?
[00:05:40] Ethan: Yes, aiming for 7/15.
[00:05:43] Amira: We'll try to get the prompts by Friday.
[00:05:47] Maya: Anything else on eval methodology — did we want to expand metrics beyond accuracy to precision/recall and a confidence calibration score?
[00:05:55] Ethan: Yes, we added calibration (ECE) and a delta-per-prompt bucket so you can see which prompts regress most. That CSV is in the drive.
[00:06:05] Sam: Quick question — you mentioned reranking latency impact?
[00:06:09] Ethan: Reranker is an extra call but can be batched; added cost but reduces false positives significantly. We'll show latency tradeoffs in the benchmark.
[00:06:18] Jia: For on-prem options, network restrictions may force us to use the Private deployment; any notes?
[00:06:23] Maya: Private supports air-gapped installs; we can share the packaging and compliance checklist. Private requires more ops lift but meets strict data residency.
[00:06:32] Amira: Okay. Anything else on guardrails?
[00:06:35] Ethan: One more thing — we've got a prototype UI for per-prompt override rules (e.g., treat certain prompt patterns as high-precision always). We'll demo next week.
[00:06:45] Sam: Nice.
[00:06:47] Maya: Alright let's move to risk and open issues. Jia?
[00:06:50] Jia: Network egress and VPC peering — we need estimated bandwidth and IP ranges for firewall rules.
[00:06:56] Ethan: We'll provide IP ranges and expected egress rates per QPS bucket.
[00:07:01] Amira: Security had one more ask — can you show proof of key management, KMS integration?
[00:07:06] Maya: We'll include KMS/HSM integration docs.
[00:07:10] Sam: Recap please?
[00:07:12] Maya: Recap: 1) Redwood: updated prompt + scoring sheet (Maya) due 7/10; 2) Redwood SE: Dedicated benchmarks with cold/warm numbers and p50/p95/p99 (Ethan) due 7/15; 3) NimbleDocs: 200 edge prompts + infra diagram (Amira/Jia) due 7/11/7/12; 4) Share SOC2 + SAML + KMS docs (Maya) by 7/11.
[00:07:36] Amira: Good. Anything else?
[00:07:38] Sam: No, thanks.
[00:07:40] Maya: Great, we'll follow up in the drive and schedule the benchmark review. Thanks all.
[00:07:45] [Call ends, recording stops]
questions: How severe is the 6% regression on long-context prompts?
Can we run Dedicated benchmarks with cold vs warm cache?
Will fallback to hosted increase costs significantly?
